exposure: birth weight category of macrosomic newborn (>= 4,500 g vs. 4,000-4,499 g)
cohort: The study participants were parturients with diabetes, at least 34.0 weeks gestational age, who delivered macrosomic newborns.
finding: Among parturients with diabetes, composite-neonatal adverse outcomes (CNAO) and shoulder dystocia were twofold higher for newborns with birthweight >= 4,500 g compared to those with birthweight 4,000-4,499 g.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery did not differ significantly between macrosomic newborns weighing >= 4,500 g and those weighing 4,000-4,499 g in parturients with diabetes.
birth_weight: 4,000 g and above (macrosomic), specifically compared at >= 4,500 g versus 4,000-4,499 g
